title: Chocolate Crêpes
changes_from_base: A small batch of batter with cocoa sifted in with the flour and a little vanilla, cooked as 18 cm crêpes and filled with chocolate-hazelnut spread instead of sugar and lemon.
summary: Delicate cocoa crêpes folded around a spoonful of chocolate-hazelnut spread for a quick, indulgent treat.

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the 118 ml milk, 1 egg, 1 tbsp sugar, 14 g melted butter, ½ tsp vanilla and ⅛ tsp salt vigorously in a bowl.

steps.title: Sift
steps.text: Sift in the 42 g flour and 1 tbsp cocoa and whisk until smooth.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Rest the batter at room temperature for at least 15 min, or overnight in the fridge.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat a small frying pan over medium heat, melt a knob of butter and spread it round, then pour in about 3 tbsp batter and swirl quickly to coat the base.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Cook undisturbed until the edges look dry, 60-90 s, then flip with a thin spatula and cook for 30-60 s more until cooked through.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Spread a teaspoon of chocolate-hazelnut spread over one quarter of each crêpe and fold in half then into quarters, or roll it up tightly.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Top with whipped cream, berries or icing sugar if you like and serve at once.

tips: Rest the batter before cooking so the crêpes turn out thin and tender rather than tough.
There's no need to grease the pan again after the first crêpe once it's seasoned with butter.
Fill and fold the crêpes while they're still warm so the filling softens slightly.
storage: Best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the pan. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
